intro: You are a field epidemiologist. Two unrelated villagers in Rampur have fever and confusion. Report to the District Health Officer first and get authorization. Talk to the doctor, Rani and Jaggu before you go to see Baba Kaladev, and visit Kamala last. Ask about travel, food and daily routine. Collect samples (the doctor collects CSF), send them to the lab, and tell the DHO which tests you ran in your final verdict.

must.hint: Dr. Verma knows when these cases began. Ask about past outbreaks in the district.

lock.msg: Get authorization from the District Health Officer first.

must.hint: You still don't know what the lab and CSF tests say about the brain and bacteria.
The waterborne theory (cholera, the broken pump) has not been properly ruled out.
Ask the patient's family whether he travelled anywhere recently.
You haven't asked the family what the patient eats and drinks.
Rani knows about other sick villagers. Earn her confidence and ask what she hears.
You haven't collected a clinical sample from Jaggu. Open Samples & Lab and collect one.

lock.msg: Speak to Rani and Jaggu before you go to meet Baba Kaladev.

must.hint: You have not yet heard what Baba Kaladev believes about the illness. Greet him respectfully and ask about the grove.

lock.msg: Meet Baba Kaladev first, then ask Rani for the discharged patient's address.

unlock.permission: Authorization granted: Community Health Center unlocked.
unlock.asha_ok: Rani (ASHA worker) can now meet you.
unlock.ward_ok: You may speak to Jaggu in the isolation ward.
unlock.sap_known: A new lead opens up. You can go back and ask the others about it.
unlock.bat_known: Another lead opens up. People you have already met may know more.

dho.name: Dr. Verma
dho.greet: You're late. Two patients, a panicking village, and my phone has not stopped ringing. Speak quickly.
dho.fallback: Speak clearly. Ask about permission, the situation, past outbreaks or resources. Or name a disease and I'll say possible or not.

topics.label: Report arrival and ask what is known so far
topics.reply: Two patients. Jaggu, 52, a farmer, is admitted at the Community Health Center. Kamala, from the west lane, was discharged yesterday and is still unwell. They are not related and live far apart. That bothers me. The village is shouting about curses and water.

topics.label: Respectfully request authorization to interview staff, patients and families
topics.reply: Fine. Permission granted. Go to the Community Health Center, start with Dr. Sharma, and do not embarrass this office. Baba Kaladev comes later: talk to Rani and the patient first.

topics.label: Demand full powers to enter any house and force testing
topics.reply: Do you think this is a police raid? Force makes families hide their sick. Ask properly or don't ask.

topics.label: Ask about past outbreaks in this district
topics.reply: Japanese encephalitis comes in the monsoon. These cases began in winter. Ask yourself what is different in winter.
ev: Cases began in winter, not in the monsoon

topics.label: Ask who the villagers trust most
topics.reply: Baba Kaladev and Rani, the ASHA worker. Baba is rude and stubborn, but half the village obeys him. Insult him and you lose them all.
ev: Baba and Rani influence the village

topics.label: Ask what lab and PPE support the district can provide
topics.reply: Samples reach the state virology lab in a day. PPE is limited; don't ask for the moon. Use the Samples & Lab desk, and tell me which tests you ran when you give your verdict.

topics.label: Say you are ready to give your final verdict
topics.reply: About time. You need linked contacts, a clear source and a lab-confirmed result. Then use the verdict button and write it yourself, including which tests you ran. No guesses.

topics.label: Ask how to test a hypothesis with him
topics.reply: Once you know the clinical picture, ask me about specific diseases. I'll say possible or not. Yes or no. Nothing more.

topics.label: Ask how many people could be at risk
topics.reply: Rampur has about 3,200 people and a market that draws three more villages. If this passes person to person, I have a district emergency. Do not let that happen.

topics.label: Apologize for the delay and promise a quick investigation
topics.reply: Save the apology. Save lives. Move.

topics.label: Ask whether other districts report similar cases
topics.reply: None. No other district has reported anything like it. So whatever this is, look for something local.
ev: No similar cases reported elsewhere; look for a local source

dho.hello: Skip the pleasantries. What do you want?

hyp.ok: YES. Possible. Fever with brain swelling, no bacteria, winter onset: it fits. Now prove the source.
hyp.weak: YES, possible. But you haven't shown me evidence yet. Go and get it.
hyp.label: Is Nipah virus possible?

hyp.reply: NO. Not possible. Nobody has diarrhoea and the lab shows no bacteria. Next.
hyp.label: Could it be cholera or typhoid?

hyp.reply: NO. The spray was weeks ago and the cattle are fine. Next.
hyp.label: Could it be pesticide poisoning?

hyp.reply: NO. It's winter. Mosquito season is over. Use your head.
hyp.label: Could it be Japanese encephalitis?

hyp.reply: NO. No animal bites, and rabies does not strike two strangers together.
hyp.label: Could it be rabies?

hyp.reply: NO. Curses do not show up in CSF.
hyp.label: Could it be a curse?

hyp.reply: NO. Wrong pattern. Fever with brain swelling and no cough cluster.
hyp.label: Could it be COVID or influenza?

hyp.reply: NO, not bacterial. The CSF shows no bacteria. Think viral.
hyp.label: Could it be bacterial meningitis?

doctor.name: Dr. Sharma
doctor.greet: Thank goodness you're here. Jaggu, 52, was admitted two days ago with high fever and confusion. A second patient, Kamala, was discharged yesterday but is still unwell. They are not related. People say it's a curse or poisoned water.
doctor.guarded: I'd rather not speculate yet. Let's build trust and gather more first.
doctor.fallback: I'm not sure I follow. Try asking about lab results, symptoms, other causes, samples or isolation.

topics.label: What do the CSF and lab results show?
topics.reply: CSF shows raised lymphocytes and protein with no bacteria. It is acute viral encephalitis: swelling of the brain.
ev: No bacteria in CSF or blood

topics.label: Have you ruled out cholera or typhoid?
topics.reply: Yes. Stool and blood tests are negative and nobody has diarrhoea. The handpump has been broken for weeks, and families boil their water anyway. It is not waterborne.

topics.label: Thank Dr. Sharma and ask how the clinic is coping
topics.reply: That means a lot. The second patient is Kamala, from the second lane past the school. She has no relation to Jaggu. We discharged her yesterday because we had no bed, but she is still not well.
ev: P1 and P2 are not relatives

topics.label: Why haven't you isolated them properly?
topics.reply: Jaggu is in the only side room. We have few masks. I can do better with district help.

topics.label: When did symptoms start? What's the timeline?
topics.reply: Fever began about 5 days ago. The families haven't given me the full story of what they ate, drank or did before that.

topics.label: What symptoms does Jaggu have besides fever?
topics.reply: Headache, vomiting, drowsiness, breathlessness, and a seizure last night. The breathing trouble worries me; this is not typical meningitis.

topics.label: Ask whether samples have gone to a virology lab
topics.reply: Only routine bloods so far. For a proper viral work-up I want fresh throat swabs and urine with PCR. You can collect swabs and urine yourself with PPE. I'll do the CSF.
ev: Samples sent to the virology lab

topics.label: Ask what worries him most
topics.reply: My staff. Two nurses handled Jaggu without masks before we suspected anything. If this spreads person to person, they are at risk.

topics.label: May I speak to Jaggu?
topics.reply: Five minutes, with a mask. He is confused, so be gentle. I'll let the ward know.

topics.label: Who can help trace contacts in the village?
topics.reply: Rani, our ASHA worker. She knows every household. She's in the clinic today; I'll introduce you.

topics.label: Ask about treatment and whether there is a cure
topics.reply: Supportive care only: fluids, oxygen, seizure control. For this kind of encephalitis there is no proven cure. Some centres have tried ribavirin, but the evidence is thin.

topics.label: Ask how dangerous this could be for the patients
topics.reply: (Quietly) Honestly? Viral encephalitis with breathing trouble can kill more than half of those who get it. I won't promise you anything about Jaggu.
ev: Encephalitis with respiratory distress carries high mortality

topics.label: Offer to help with paperwork or a night shift
reply: Really? (A tired laugh) Thank you. I haven't slept properly in two days.
Take the register on the desk. Every visitor to Jaggu's bed is written in it. It might help your contact list.

topics.label: Ask what the history sheet says about travel and food
topics.reply: Almost nothing. 'Resident of Rampur', that's all. You will have to ask the families yourself: travel, milk, vegetables, fruit, meat, how they cook.
ev: Clinic history lacks travel and food details

doctor.hello: Yes, hello. Please be quick, I have patients waiting.

asha_worker.name: Rani

lock.msg: Dr. Sharma should introduce you to Rani first.

asha_worker.greet: Namaste. Dr. Sharma said you would come. I know every house in Rampur. How can I help?
asha_worker.guarded: People are scared. I can't say more until they trust you.
asha_worker.fallback: Hmm? Ask me about the villagers, sap customs, the sugarcane spray, Baba-ji, or Kamala.

topics.label: Ask what she is hearing in the community
topics.reply: Two families in the east hamlet have young men bedridden with fever. They won't come here because Baba-ji said hospital needles will kill them.
ev: Unreported fever cases in east hamlet

topics.label: Could the sugarcane pesticide spray be the cause?
topics.reply: The spray was three weeks ago. Farmhands and cattle are fine. Only a few people are sick, and not all of them farm.
ev: Spray timing and spread don't fit

topics.label: Demand a list of everyone who is sick, now
topics.reply: If you push like that, families will hide their sick even more. Please don't make me choose between you and my neighbours.

topics.label: Ask how to win over Baba Kaladev
topics.reply: Respect him first. Don't argue about the curse. Ask about the sacred grove; he watches it every night.

topics.label: Ask for Kamala's address so you can visit her
topics.reply: Second lane past the primary school, blue gate. Kamala is home, weak and forgetful, and her son Mohan is with her. Wear a mask and be gentle.

topics.label: Ask what villagers usually eat and drink in winter
topics.reply: Rice, dal, vegetables from kitchen gardens, packet milk from the dairy booth. Tea all day. Most families boil their water. Nothing different this winter, as far as I know.
ev: Usual village diet reviewed; nothing unusual reported

topics.label: Ask how families are coping and what they need
topics.reply: They fear losing wages. Vikram's wife says he has a cough and fever now, and she moved the children to her mother's.
ev: A neighbour of the index case now has fever and cough

topics.label: Ask who has been caring for the patients
topics.reply: Jaggu's daughter Lakshmi nursed him at home for two days. Nobody wore masks, and she cleaned his vomit by hand.

topics.label: Ask how she is holding up herself
reply: (Looks down) Honestly? I'm frightened. I went to Jaggu's house on the first day without a mask.
But if I stop, who will go door to door? Thank you for asking.
ev: ASHA worker visited index household unprotected

topics.label: Ask if animals or birds have been seen near the places patients go
topics.reply: Not the cattle. But the temple boys say bats have been dropping half-eaten fruit around the grove this winter. They sweep it every morning.
ev: Bats and half-eaten fruit reported around the grove

topics.label: Ask whether anyone travelled recently or had visitors
topics.reply: Nobody has travelled far. A wedding party visited from the next district two weeks ago, but nobody there is sick and none of our patients went.
ev: No travel or visitor link to the cases

topics.label: Ask about the drink sold at the bus stand in winter
topics.reply: Ah, the sweet palm sap. In winter men tap the palms at night and leave pots to fill. Vikram sells it at the bus stand at dawn. People drink it raw, cold and sweet.
ev: Raw palm sap sold and drunk fresh at dawn in winter

topics.label: Ask how most families cook and store food
topics.reply: Wood-fire stoves. Rice and vegetables are boiled or fried, milk is boiled twice, leftovers are kept covered. The only things eaten raw are fruit and salad.
ev: Food is cooked thoroughly; water is boiled

asha_worker.hello: Namaste. Tell me how I can help.

patient_1.name: Jaggu (Patient 1)

lock.msg: Ask Dr. Sharma for permission to speak to Jaggu in the isolation ward.

patient_1.greet: Please be gentle. Papa is very weak. I will speak for him when he cannot.
patient_1.fallback: (Jaggu mumbles.) Ask about what I ate... or when I fell ill.

topics.label: Gently ask what he ate or drank in the days before he fell ill
reply: (Weak) Rice, dal... what Lakshmi cooked. Tea. Nothing different. My head... I can't remember properly.

reply.text: He goes out to the fields before dawn and eats breakfast late. I don't know what he has on the way.

ev: Usual home-cooked diet; nothing unusual recalled

topics.label: Did anyone share handpump water with you?
topics.reply: My family used the old pump sometimes. But I felt sick before that... the water is not it.

topics.label: Ask Lakshmi whether Jaggu ever drinks anything sold at the bus stand
topics.reply: Yes... now that you ask. Papa buys a cup of the sweet palm sap from Vikram at the bus stand when he goes to the market, a few times a week. I forgot because it's just a drink.
ev: Index case also drank raw palm sap
P1 and P2 both bought sap from Vikram
Vikram sells raw sap to many customers

topics.label: Order him to stay strictly in bed
topics.reply: Please don't shout. He is very sick and frightened.

topics.label: Ask about family and who stayed close this week
topics.reply: My daughter Lakshmi stayed with me. Neighbours came and held my hand.

topics.label: Ask Jaggu whether he noticed anything odd near the tree where the sap is sold
topics.reply: Now I remember... the pot was sticky, with chewed fruit bits and something like bite marks. Wings were flapping above before sunrise. I didn't think about it.
ev: Chewed fruit and bite marks near sap pots

topics.label: When did he first feel unwell?
topics.reply: Headache and fever came suddenly, five days ago. Then I started forgetting things.

topics.label: Ask Lakshmi whether she has eaten or rested
topics.reply: No... I haven't left his side. Thank you for asking. I've had a small cough since yesterday, but it's nothing.

topics.label: Ask what Jaggu does for work and his daily routine

reply.text: I farm two acres near the grove. Paddy, some vegetables. I wake before dawn.
Papa also helps Vikram with his morning work sometimes, for a cup of tea.

ev: Index case is out before dawn most days

topics.label: Ask whether Jaggu travelled anywhere in the last month
topics.reply: Papa hasn't left Rampur. The farthest he goes is the Sunday market in town, eight kilometres away by bus.
ev: No travel outside the area in the last month

topics.label: Ask which milk and dairy products the family uses
topics.reply: Packet milk from the dairy booth. We boil it twice, and Papa takes it with his tea. No raw milk, and we have no cattle at home.

topics.label: Ask which vegetables and fruits he eats
topics.reply: Vegetables from our kitchen garden: brinjal, gourd, greens, all cooked. Bananas from the market, peeled. Sometimes a guava.
ev: Cooked garden vegetables; peeled market fruit

topics.label: Ask whether he ate meat, fish or eggs recently
topics.reply: Chicken curry at my aunt's house ten days ago. Everyone ate it and nobody is sick. Eggs only boiled. No fish this month.
ev: Chicken eaten well cooked; no one else ill

topics.label: Ask how food is cooked and stored at home
topics.reply: On a wood stove. Everything is boiled or fried, and nothing is eaten raw except fruit. Leftovers are kept covered, and we boil the drinking water.
ev: Food is cooked thoroughly; water is boiled

patient_2.name: Kamala (Patient 2)
patient_2.greet: Please come in. Amma gets dizzy if she stands. The doctor sent her home because there was no bed.
patient_2.guarded: I... don't remember... please, not now.
patient_2.fallback: (Kamala rubs her forehead.) Ask me about how I feel, the sap, the visitors, or Jaggu.

topics.label: Ask how she is feeling and offer her a seat
topics.reply: Headaches, dizziness, and I forget words. I'm scared they'll take me back to the ward.

topics.label: Ask what Kamala usually eats and drinks in a week
reply: Rice, dal, vegetables, boiled milk, some fruit. And sometimes, in winter, I buy a cup of the sweet palm sap at the bus stand. Vikram sells it at dawn.
I last had it five days before the fever began.
ev: Drank raw date palm sap about 5 days before onset

topics.label: When did her symptoms begin?
topics.reply: Fever and a terrible headache a few days later. Then I did not recognise my own son.
ev: Onset about 4 to 5 days after exposure

topics.label: Ask whether she knows or is related to Jaggu
topics.reply: Jaggu? I only know his face from the market. We are not related, and I have never been to his house.
ev: P1 and P2 never had direct contact

topics.label: Tell her she must go back to hospital immediately
topics.reply: (Starts crying) No... I just came home. Please don't send me back.

topics.label: Offer a home check with Dr. Sharma and a mask
topics.reply: Yes... that would help. I would feel safer. I'll wear the mask for the family.

topics.label: Ask Mohan how he has been caring for her
topics.reply: I cleaned her when she vomited and held her through the seizures. No gloves, no mask. I have had a headache since last night.
ev: Caregiver exposed to patient's body fluids

topics.label: Who has visited since she came home?
topics.reply: Neighbours and my aunt. They all touched her face and cried.

topics.label: Ask what Kamala does for a living and where she goes daily

reply.text: I stitch blouses at home. Every morning I walk to the bus stand to deliver orders.
She stops at the stalls there on the way back.

ev: Kamala passes the bus stand stalls daily

topics.label: Ask Mohan if he is okay and eating properly
topics.reply: I'm fine... just worried. I haven't gone to college since Amma fell ill. Thank you for asking.

topics.label: Ask Mohan whether he noticed anything unusual where Amma buys the sap
topics.reply: Yes. Near the bus stand there's a tall palm tree with pots tied to it. In the evenings I've seen big bats hanging in it and flying around. Once I saw one licking at a pot.
ev: Fruit bats seen at the palm tree near the bus stand
Bats lick the open sap pots

topics.label: Ask Kamala about travel in the last month
topics.reply: Nowhere. Only the bus stand and the market. I haven't left Rampur in years.
ev: No travel outside the area in the last month

topics.label: Ask how she cooks and stores food
topics.reply: On a wood stove. Everything is boiled or fried, milk is boiled twice, and leftovers are kept covered.
ev: Food is cooked thoroughly; water is boiled

baba.name: Baba Kaladev
baba.greet: Another city fool with needles! Get out of my grove!
baba.guarded: You haven't earned a word from me. Get lost.
baba.fallback: Speak plainly, fool, or leave. Ask about the grove, the sick, or the sap.

topics.label: Respectfully thank Baba-ji and ask about the grove
topics.reply: (Grudgingly) Hmph. At least you speak like a human. The grove has been disturbed. Since the trees were cut, the village has fallen sick. Don't think I like you.
ev: Curse belief; trees cut near grove

topics.label: Ask if he has noticed any animals at the grove at night
topics.reply: Fine, since you bowed properly. The big night-bats nest in those palms in huge numbers. They eat the fruit and drink from the sap pots left overnight. Now stop pestering me.
ev: Fruit bats roost in grove palms
Bats drink from open sap pots

topics.label: Tell him the curse is dangerous misinformation
topics.reply: You dare, you arrogant fool! Get out of my grove before I curse your whole family!

topics.label: Ask him to tell villagers the clinic is safe
topics.reply: Hmph. If you honour the grove, I'll tell them the clinic is no enemy. Not for you. For them. The hidden ones will come.

topics.label: Ask him to tell the story of the sacred grove
topics.reply: My ancestors planted these palms for the goddess. A greedy contractor cut trees for the new road, and the bats lost their trees and came here. You city people understand nothing.
ev: Habitat loss pushed bats into grove

topics.label: Ask when he first noticed villagers falling sick
topics.reply: A week ago Jaggu came to me burning with fever. I gave him herbs. Don't look at me like that, I did what I could.
ev: Jaggu ill about a week ago

topics.label: Ask who collects the sap and how it is stored
topics.reply: Vikram taps at night and leaves the pots open under the crowns until dawn, then sells them at the bus stand. People pay good money for it, fools.
ev: Open pots left under palms overnight

topics.label: Ask for his blessing and help to reach hidden families
topics.reply: Hmph. Go with my blessing. I'll send word to the east hamlet. The sick can go to your clinic, and I will pray for them. Now leave.

topics.label: Offer a donation for the temple and ask what it needs
topics.reply: Hmph. A few rupees don't buy me. But the roof leaks. ...Maybe you are not like the last doctor.

topics.label: Ask whether something like this ever happened here before
topics.reply: Twenty years ago, some boys died of brain fever after eating fruit from the grove. Nobody connected anything. Nobody asked me.
ev: Earlier unexplained deaths linked to grove fruit

baba.hello: What do you want, outsider? Be quick.

hints.#FruitBatRoost: Someone close to a patient may have noticed something unusual near a tree on the patients' daily route. Listen to the family members who walk the same paths.
hints.#NonBacterial: Ask Dr. Sharma what the tests rule out.
hints.#BodyFluidExposure: Find out who nursed the patients and how closely.
hints.#NipahPCRPositive: No laboratory confirmation yet. Collect a throat swab, urine or CSF, request an RT-PCR in Samples & Lab, and meet everyone involved so the lab can report.
hints.#Sampled_P2: You haven't collected a sample from Kamala yet.
hints.#RawDatePalmSap: You have not yet found what the patients had in common. Ask about food, drink and daily routine, especially from the last patient you meet.

plan.t: Ban or avoid raw sap; advise boiling or discarding
plan.label: Stop the source

plan.t: Cover sap pots/trees with bamboo skirts or nets against bats
plan.label: Keep bats away from the source

plan.t: Isolate cases and trace contacts, including hidden cases
plan.label: Isolate and trace contacts

plan.t: Infection control and PPE for health workers and caregivers
plan.label: Protect health workers

plan.t: Community engagement with Baba, Rani and families
plan.label: Work with the community

harm.t: Spraying insecticide as the main response

p1.msg: Fine. I'll do a fresh lumbar puncture with aseptic precautions and give you 2 mL for virology. Mask up.

p2.msg: No. Kamala is recovering at home. A repeat lumbar puncture isn't justified.

p1.msg: A biopsy isn't indicated in a living encephalitis patient. Tissue is for post-mortem work-ups. Throat, urine and CSF will tell you more.

p2.msg: Not indicated. She is recovering. Use swabs and urine.

p1.msg: He isn't intubated, so there's nothing to aspirate. Use throat or nasopharyngeal swabs instead.

p2.msg: She isn't on a ventilator. No.

serum: IgM equivocal, IgG negative (early illness; repeat on a later sample)

fungal.txt: No growth at 7 days (final report at 14 days)

tb.txt: AFB smear negative. M. tuberculosis not detected.

bioc.txt: Mildly raised ALT/AST, normal creatinine. Non-specific.

serum: Mildly raised ALT/AST, sodium 131 (low), creatinine normal. Non-specific.

cbc.txt: Platelets low-normal, mild leukopenia. Viral pattern.

edta: Platelets 108,000 (low), WBC 3,600 (low), no neutrophilia. Viral pattern.

csfchem.txt: Lymphocytic pleocytosis (48 cells/uL), raised protein, normal glucose. Viral encephalitis pattern.

stoolrm.txt: No ova, cysts, pus cells or blood

na.lesion: There are no skin lesions to swab.

schedule.text: Another young man in the east hamlet falls ill with fever and confusion.
Two people who shop at the bus stand in the early morning develop fever.
A nurse who handled Jaggu without a mask develops fever.
Two neighbours who nursed the patients are admitted with fever.
Three more people from Jaggu's lane fall ill.
Two temple boys who sweep the grove develop fever.
A cluster of three cases appears in the east hamlet.
Three family members of earlier cases fall ill.

vars.label: Worked in sugarcane fields during spraying
Had contact with a sick person
Ate fruit picked from grove trees

actions.label: Public advisory: do not drink raw date palm sap
actions.say: The advisory goes out through ASHA workers, the temple loudspeaker and the school.

actions.label: Install bamboo skirts on the sap pots in the grove
actions.say: Bats can no longer reach the sap pots.

actions.label: Isolate the east hamlet cases and start contact tracing
actions.say: ASHA workers begin daily visits to every contact.

actions.label: Barrier nursing and PPE for the clinic staff
actions.say: Nurses now use masks, gowns and gloves on the ward.

actions.label: Chlorinate the handpump and declare the water safe

adds.text: Villagers relaxed after the 'water is safe' message while the real source kept spreading the illness.

actions.say: The pump is cleaned, but the real source is untouched.

actions.label: Spray insecticide across the village
actions.say: Villagers panic about chemicals. Nothing changes for the outbreak.

actions.label: Cull the fruit bats in the grove

adds.text: Disturbed bats dispersed to new roosts and contaminated more sap pots.

actions.say: Baba is furious and the village is shaken.

pool.title: A journalist is on the phone
pool.text: A local reporter has heard about 'brain fever' in Rampur and wants a statement before the evening bulletin.

options.label: Give a short, factual briefing
options.say: The report is calm and accurate. The village feels respected.

options.label: Say 'no comment'
options.say: The story runs anyway, filled with rumours.

options.label: Say it is probably Nipah virus

cases.text: A family hides a sick relative after the panic and he is found late.

options.say: Panic spreads and families begin hiding the sick.

pool.title: A politician demands answers
pool.text: The local MLA's office calls: 'When will this be over? The district is losing patience.'

options.label: Give an honest update with no promises
options.say: He grumbles but accepts the facts.

options.label: Promise it will be over in two days

later.say: The two-day promise is broken. The village stops believing the official team.

options.label: Refuse to take the call
options.say: The politician complains to the DHO about you.

pool.title: A suspected case in the next village
pool.text: A health worker reports a man with fever and confusion in Kolur, six kilometres away. He sells vegetables at the Rampur market twice a week.

options.label: Send a team now (₹3,000, 4 hours)
options.say: The patient is isolated early and his family is traced.

options.label: Ask the local ASHA to monitor by phone (₹200)

cases.text: The patient's family members fall ill in Kolur.

options.say: A phone check is not enough to stop the spread.

options.label: Ignore it for now

cases.text: A cluster appears in Kolur village.

options.say: You decide to focus on Rampur.

pool.title: PPE shortage
pool.text: The clinic storekeeper reports that masks and gowns are running low.

options.label: Borrow 8 kits from the district hospital (3 hours)
Reuse cloth masks and carry on
options.say: Staff continue unprotected. A biosafety lapse is recorded.

options.label: Pause fieldwork for a day (24 hours)
options.say: Safe, but the outbreak does not wait.

pool.title: A rumour spreads on WhatsApp
pool.text: A message claims that the hospital injects patients with poison. Families are talking about leaving.

options.label: Ask Baba and Rani to speak at the grove (2 hours)
options.say: Their calm words spread faster than the rumour.

options.label: Ignore it
options.say: The rumour grows and trust falls.
